found_values.value: 900 ms for one main-loop pass while the USB host takes nothing; no bound while the host keeps accepting data more slowly than it is written. A pass holds at most one flash window: out_store_tick() (main.c:1049) erases or programs once, and out_store_reclaim() runs only on a pass where the tick did nothing (main.c:1083). The longest window is one 4 kB sector erase, 400 ms maximum (W25Q16JV-DTR revision I, tSE, a packaged-part figure; the die's figure is not known). A printf follows the window in the same pass (main.c:1059-1086), and can_report() prints every 3,000 ms (main.c:598-601, :1089). pico-sdk 2.3.1 stdio_usb_out_chars() (stdio_usb.c:102-132, byte-identical in 2.3.0) blocks until PICO_STDIO_USB_STDOUT_TIMEOUT_US has passed since the last accepted write; the default is 500,000 us (stdio_usb.h:31-33), and the firmware does not override it. After that timeout a later write in the same pass returns at once, because last_avail_time is static. 400 ms + 500 ms = 900 ms. Each accepted write restarts the 500 ms, so a slow reader sets no bound. The boot loop erases up to OUT_STORE_SECTORS = 2 sectors before can_start() (main.c:937-942, out_store.h:122): 800 ms plus prints, before any watchdog the image might start

USB 2.0 section 7.1.6.1: the upstream-facing port of a full-speed device with a detachable cable may have 100 pF (CINUB), 'comprised of up to 75 pF of lumped capacitance to ground on each line at the transceiver and in the connector and an additional 25 pF capacitance on each conductor in the transmission line between the receptacle and the transceiver. report.value: 13 errata affect stepping A4 (CHIP_ID.REVISION 0x8): E1, E2, E4, E5, E6, E7, E8, E11, E12, E17, E26, E27, E28. None constrains a pin, a pull resistor or an input front end on A4: E9 (increased Bank 0 leakage with the pad input enabled, pull-down weaker than the leakage) affects A2 only and is fixed in A3; E3 (QFN-60 GPIO_NSMASK) and E16 (USB_OTP_VDD and OTP reads) are A2 only. Those that constrain a peripheral: RP2350-E5 (DMA): aborting a channel can fire its CHAIN_TO and re-trigger it; workaround: clear CHx_CTRL_TRIG.EN of the aborted channel and of any channel it chains to before the abort; cited by firmware/iomcu/src/out_ppm.c:69. RP2350-E8 (DMA): CHAIN_TO may not fire after a zero-length transfer; avoid zero-length transfers with CHAIN_TO. RP2350-E12 (USB), 'RP2350 A2, RP2350 A3, RP2350 A4 (mitigated on A3)': events are not reliably registered when clk_sys is equal to or slower than clk_usb; workaround: 'Run clk_sys faster than clk_usb by at least 10% when the peripheral is in use', at least 52.8 MHz with clk_usb at the 48 MHz section 12.7.3.1 requires; reset, suspend and resume signalling is exempt. (Section 12.7.3.1's note says only '> 48MHz'; the erratum's 10 % governs.) RP2350-E27 (bus fabric): BUS_PRIORITY bits are mis-wired on the FASTPERI and APB arbiters; no complete fix. RP2350-E2 (SIO): writes to SIO offsets 0x180 to 0x1fc release spinlocks 0x80 below; pico-sdk uses software locks on RP2350; locks 5, 6, 7, 10, 11 and 18 to 31 do not alias. RP2350-E1 (SIO interpolator): OVERF flag broken by right-rotate. RP2350-E11 (XIP cache): clean by set/way retags dirty lines; pico-sdk xip_cache_clean_all() applies the workaround. Core and debug only: E4 (RISC-V SBA stalls with core 1 in clock-gated sleep), E6 (Hazard3 PMPCFG RWX transposed), E7 (Hazard3 U-mode ignores no mstatus.mie). OTP and security: E17 (guarded read of a single ECC row faults if the adjacent row is not valid ECC), E28 (OTP keys for pages 62/63 apply to all lock words), E26 (RCP random delays side channel)

report.value: The RP2350 watchdog counts down in microseconds from LOAD (24 bits, max 0xffffff, about 16.8 s, Table 1249), is disabled at reset (CTRL.ENABLE 0x0) and pauses while either core is in debug or JTAG accesses the bus (PAUSE_DBG0, PAUSE_DBG1, PAUSE_JTAG reset 1, Table 1248). The image sets no timeout (V4), against the owner's decision that it enables one (2026-09-25). Checked against the stop deadline found for V1 (200 ms) and the longest legitimate stall found for V2 (900 ms: one 400 ms packaged-part sector erase plus one 500 ms blocked USB write): no timeout exceeds the stall and meets the deadline. The 400 ms erase alone exceeds 200 ms, and so does the boot loop's two-sector erase (800 ms). A conflict for the owner, not a defect of the part. The tree offers no way out: pico-sdk's flash_range_erase() holds the core for the whole erase; the packaged W25Q16JV documents Erase/Program Suspend, not used by the tree and not analysed
